decisions.question: S22 reversed root D4: nidana.runtime becomes a leaf-parent (about twelve phases over ten internal slices) instead of an internal node with children. The two leading options (leaf-parent; or two children nidana.runtime.bus and nidana.runtime.topology joined by an internal contract) produce different nodes and contracts, and the Specification is silent. Is this the tree-shape run-stop?

options.label: Not a stop; accept the leaf-parent
options.consequence: nidana.runtime is phase-planned directly; no internal contract and no ADR amendment; the root's D4 prose and conventions example are restated at the root refresh. A later hsdd-spec run can still decompose it if the phase plan shows it cannot be kept to independent, window-sized phases.

options.label: Not a stop; force the two-child split
options.consequence: Needs ADR-001 item 2 amended so an internal contract's fixtures may import lib/src/, one internal contract step, two phase plans; the contract freezes the read-stage seam that three experiments had to patch on both sides.

options.label: Stop the run
options.consequence: The owner decides the runtime's shape; every runtime-dependent phase plan waits.

decisions.chosen: Not a stop; accept the leaf-parent
decisions.why: The run reads the shape stop as holding only when neither option has a stated reason to lead (DEC-002). Here accepted governance gives one: ADR-001 item 2 forbids fixtures that import src/, ADR-002 item 3 allows exactly two public libraries, and bus-api@v1 with bus-testing@v1 must share one library (TestBus extends the final Bus), so any internal contract between runtime children could never become stable under the run's own final gate; ADR-001 item 10 with fp-progression then puts both contracts' declarations in one leaf-parent's first phase. HSDD's leaf-parent rule holds (one owner; phases fit one review window). The counter-signal is HSDD's tip to add a level once a leaf-parent passes a handful of phases; twelve is past that, which is why confidence is medium. The reversal changes no root contract, and a later decomposition stays possible, so the choice is reversible at the cost of re-planning one node.
evidence: ~/git/hsdd/docs/users-guide.md (Tips: add a level, do not widen)
